speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To begin, how long have you been trying to conceive, and would you describe your menstrual cycles as regular or irregular?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pelvic floor tension and dyspareunia are concerning; have you noticed any pain specifically during urination or bowel movements, or any abnormal vaginal discharge? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, CBC, and Cervical_Cytology.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Normal; CBC: WBC 6,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL; Cervical_Cytology: No specimen obtained due to patient's pelvic floor muscles tensing up and discomfort during attempted speculum examination.
